title: SNAP entry and exit sit beside resource and person-earnings changes while job counts usually remain unchanged
source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent reference-month SNAP transition with monthly household resource, person-earnings, and job-count context

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric THINCPOV in both months

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive transition context using WPFINWGT at month t and REPWGT1–REPWGT240; THINCPOV is monthly and categories are classified as down, same, or up.
observations.uncertainty: Rare transition and selected valid context universe; intervals describe sampling uncertainty and do not establish SNAP impact.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt between adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Resource decline may precede or accompany program entry; it is not caused by entry.

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric THINCPOV in both months

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR transition-context method as the no-to-yes observation.
observations.uncertainty: Rare transition and selected valid context universe; intervals describe sampling uncertainty and do not establish that exit caused resource decline.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting reported SNAP receipt between adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exit may reflect income, renewal, administrative, reporting, household, or other changes; the result is not an exit-to-work measure.

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric RMNUMJOBS in both months

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive transition context using monthly RMNUMJOBS categories.
observations.uncertainty: Job-count universe is smaller than the full transition universe and does not measure hours, pay, quality, schedule, or choice.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt with valid monthly job counts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable job count is not stable work quality or security; job count does not establish an exit-to-work pathway.

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric RMNUMJOBS in both months

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR monthly job-count transition-context method as the no-to-yes observation.
observations.uncertainty: Job-count universe is selected and coarse; intervals do not establish that exit caused job stability or loss.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting reported SNAP receipt with valid monthly job counts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable job count does not show stable earnings, hours, benefits, schedule control, or restored material security.

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric TPEARN in both months; earnings universe is narrower than the transition universe

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive transition context using monthly person earnings TPEARN, WPFINWGT at month t, and REPWGT1–REPWGT240; categories are down, same, or up.
observations.uncertainty: The valid earnings universe is selected and small; TPEARN is person earnings, not household income, hours, pay rate, work quality, or job stability. Intervals describe sampling uncertainty and do not establish SNAP impact.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt with numeric monthly person earnings in both adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Earnings can move because of days in the month, timing, job composition, hours, reporting, or other changes; a decline around entry is not evidence that SNAP caused lost earnings.

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric TPEARN in both months; earnings universe is narrower than the transition universe

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR monthly person-earnings transition-context method as the no-to-yes observation.
observations.uncertainty: The valid earnings universe is selected and small; the result does not measure household resources, hours, pay rate, work quality, or why SNAP ended. Intervals do not establish that exit caused earnings recovery.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting reported SNAP receipt with numeric monthly person earnings in both adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Earnings increases can reflect return timing, composition, reporting, or other income/work changes; they are not an exit-to-work measure or proof of restored household security.

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric TMWKHRS in both months; monthly-hours universe is limited to people with a job in at least one reference month

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive transition context using monthly average hours TMWKHRS, WPFINWGT at month t, and REPWGT1–REPWGT240; categories are down, same, or up.
observations.uncertainty: Selected job-holder universe; TMWKHRS is average weekly hours at all jobs in the reference month, not a schedule-control or pay measure. Intervals do not establish SNAP impact.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt with numeric monthly average hours in both adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable hours can coexist with lower earnings, job loss outside the valid universe, poor job quality, or worsening household resources; hours are not an exit-to-work measure.

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs with numeric TMWKHRS in both months; monthly-hours universe is limited to people with a job in at least one reference month

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR monthly-hours transition-context method as the no-to-yes observation.
observations.uncertainty: Selected job-holder universe; TMWKHRS does not measure earnings, hours desired, schedule control, job quality, or why SNAP ended. Intervals do not establish that exit caused stable hours.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting reported SNAP receipt with numeric monthly average hours in both adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable hours around exit do not prove restored earnings or security; they may coexist with other changes in pay, household resources, or program administration.

related_sources.claim: The reproduction audit preserves the resource, earnings, and job-context input hashes, row counts, matched transition pairs, and Fay-BRR method.
The hours audit preserves the v16 monthly-hours input hash, output hash, row counts, matched transition pairs, and Fay-BRR method.

boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive context comparison around selected person-level SNAP transitions. It does not estimate SNAP effects, household benefit spells, notice/effort/remedy, exact bills, food security, desired hours, pay rate, work quality, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Person records may represent covered members of a SNAP unit. THINCPOV is monthly household income-to-poverty ratio; TPEARN is monthly person earnings; TMWKHRS is monthly average hours among job holders; RMNUMJOBS is monthly job count. Their valid universes are separate and none alone measures restored household security.
